title: a job is removed from the language, by receipt or by tag, and the removing half takes a capability
scope:
the two members that remove rows from the queue's tables, the `tag` column they select on,
and the capability that gates them. It decides no retention *policy* — no default lifetime, no
sweeper of the runtime's own, no `[queue]` key that expires anything — and it changes nothing about
how a job is claimed, retried or dead-lettered.

summary.headline: A job can be deleted by receipt or purged by tag, and both need a capability
summary.body:
`Core\Queue::delete` removes the one job named by its receipt, and `Core\Queue::purge` removes a
population chosen by state, by a tag written at push time, or by age, always under a limit that
is finite even when nothing is written. Finished jobs are the default set. A job currently being
worked can never be removed, and a dead job only when the call names that state, so no record of
a failure disappears without a line of source saying so. Both members take the deny-by-default
`queue.purge` capability; pushing, checking, cancelling and counting still take none.
